analysis.title: Prime Perspective: Spike in ETF Shorts
key_insights: Global Fundamental L/S hedge funds fell -1.3% on 11/5 (a -2 SD move), driven mainly by market/beta exposure. YTD performance is +8.7%.
TMT L/S funds fell more than -4% and are roughly flat to slightly positive YTD, down from about +24% before the June/July AI sell-off. US-focused funds fell -1.7% and are up 5.5% YTD.

Systematic L/S managers rose +0.2% (gains in the U.S. and EM Asia offset losses in Europe and DM Asia) and are up +16% YTD. Multi-Strats fell -1.4% on high-beta names, Info Tech, Momentum (down 3.7 SD) and negative idiosyncratic returns.

GS Vol Panic Index surged to 9.57 out of 10, back in the panic zone (9.5+). The ~5pt rise was the 3rd largest daily jump ever, following Wednesday's drop (4th largest ever). The two-day swing was the largest on record.
VVIX had its 2nd largest one-day increase ever, behind only Volmageddon in Feb '18. Cboe put volume exceeded 11mm contracts, a record, surpassing the prior high in Apr '25.

Equity drawdown was led by tech: NDX -6.4% (worst day since 3/16/20), R2K -4.5% (worst since 4/3/25), SPX -4.4% (worst since 4/4/25). Many GS AI baskets had their biggest down day since the launch of ChatGPT.
Prime flows showed more hedging via Macro Products but, on a single-stock basis, no sign of panic or faster de-grossing. GS concludes discretionary HFs were not the main driver of the price action.
US-listed ETF shorts rose +7% on 11/5, the largest 1-day increase since March and the third largest in five years, led by Large Cap Equity ETFs.

Global equities were de-grossed for a 4th straight session (8 of the last 9), but the pace was modest (-0.5 SD vs 1-year). Net selling was the largest in two weeks (-1.6 SD), with long and short sales at 2.2 to 1.

Nearly all major regions were net sold except DM Asia, led by EM Asia (Taiwan, Korea, China), North America and Europe. 7 of 11 global sectors were net sold, led by Info Tech, Consumer Disc and Industrials. Energy, Financials (short covers) and Real Estate were the most net bought.

Global AI stocks (GSXGGLAI constituents) were net sold for a 6th straight session (-2.6 SD, 1-year), driven by long and short sales at 2.2 to 1. The trailing 20-day pace of HF selling in global AI stocks is the largest in more than five years (-3.0 SD, 5-year).

Gross leverage fell -0.7 pts to 314.2% (85th percentile 1-year, 97th percentile 5-year). Net leverage fell -1.5 pts to 71.8% (4th percentile 1-year, 37th percentile 5-year). Gross leverage has risen month/month because fund equity fell faster than gross market value after performance losses.
risk_factors: Further hedge fund performance erosion after a challenging October, with TMT L/S funds down from about +24% YTD before the June/July AI sell-off to roughly flat.
Continued de-grossing, especially in global AI stocks, which have been net sold for six straight sessions.
Rising ETF shorting and record put volumes point to stress, though single-stock Prime flows did not show panic.
Gross leverage ratio is elevated (97th percentile 5-year) because fund equity is falling faster than gross market value.

tension_points.bull_case: Single-stock Prime flows show no panic and no acceleration of de-grossing. De-grossing was modest (-0.5 SD), so discretionary HFs were not the main driver of the sell-off.
tension_points.bear_case: Vol Panic Index, VVIX, record put volumes and the largest ETF short increase since March point to market stress. AI stock selling by HFs is the largest in more than five years on a 20-day basis.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Single-stock flows turning to an accelerated de-grossing pace above the recent run rate.

theme_stances.key_argument: Prime flows show hedging via Macro Products and ETF shorts, but single-stock flows do not show panic or faster de-grossing, so discretionary HFs were not the main driver.
theme_stances.evidence: they do NOT point to signs of panic and an acceleration of de-grossing
